- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.00) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; dampen next period’s forecast by 1–3%.
- Model consistently overpredicts in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 1–2% for first 5 days.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +1.00 to -0.33), model often lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment shift.
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive days below 65), model tends to hold or overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model often overfits recent trends; apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility in forecast.
